round_summary.round_hypothesis: For a small (690-sample) sarcasm dataset with BERT+SVM features, label-preserving surface-level paraphrasing and lexical noise on the training text will improve fold-averaged weighted F1 by regularizing sentence embeddings; the key open questions are (a) which component to perturb (utterance vs. context vs. both) and (b) how strong the perturbation may be before sarcasm cues (intonation words, intensifiers, negations, contrastive framing) are destroyed.
round_summary.exploration_objective: Probe one perturbation axis per candidate across a 2x-4x multiplier band: synonym substitution, contextual (masked-LM) word replacement, back-translation paraphrase, random word-order/deletion noise, context-only perturbation, context-window resampling, speaker-token normalization, and a low-cost/high-cost runtime contrast, so that each fold-F1 change can be attributed to a single factor.
round_summary.strategy_selection_rationale: All candidates are single-operation (or two ops only where a paraphrase must be paired with an explicit sarcasm-cue protection filter), operate on raw training text before BERT feature extraction, and copy the original sarcasm label plus speaker/context_speakers alignment to every generated replica, so label semantics are preserved. Strengths are deliberately conservative (5-20% token change rates) except for one intentional high-strength arm and one word-order-destruction control, which bracket the usable perturbation range. Cheap ops (synonym, deletion) and expensive ops (back-translation, MLM) are both represented to expose the F1-vs-processing-time trade-off. Augmentation is applied only to training folds; validation folds stay original.

round_summary.round_hypothesis: Round 0's leading hypothesis - that uniform full-corpus label-preserving paraphrase raises weighted F1 - was left unresolved (best arm P04 +0.0016, inside sibling seed noise; all other replication arms within ~0.002 of the 0.7130 baseline). This round tests the successor hypothesis that WHICH rows are copied and WHAT NEW INFORMATION is injected matters more than the operator strength: gains should come from (a) selective augmentation targeted at decision-boundary-relevant rows, (b) cross-example / external-model content that adds genuinely new utterance-context pairs rather than near-duplicates, and (c) label-conditioned edits that sharpen rather than dilute the utterance-context incongruity signal.
round_summary.exploration_objective: Cover mechanisms and information sources untouched in round 0 - model state (SVM margin), cross-example recombination, external generative models, label-conditioned sentiment editing, and in-distribution speaker identity substitution - while carrying forward one conservative refinement of the only favourable motif (back-translation) and one control that isolates the selection criterion from the operator. All conclusions from round 0 are treated as provisional (single-seed exploration stage); no family is retired, including the harmful speaker-anonymization family, which is revisited in a repaired, in-distribution form.
round_summary.strategy_selection_rationale: Follow-up on round 0 hypothesis: partially supported at best - the paraphrase family is unresolved (favourable direction, magnitude inside noise) and the 'perturbation ceiling' sub-result is confounded by the fact that validation folds were never transformed. Budget: 5 of 7 arms open previously untested families (selective/model-state, cross-example grafting, external LLM generation, incongruity amplification), 1 is a matched control that separates 'hard-row selection' from 'operator', 1 is a conservative refinement of back-translation with multi-pivot diversity, and 1 repairs the speaker-identity family in a form that keeps augmented text in the corpus's own surface distribution. All arms respect the 2-4x multiplier, act on raw text before BERT feature extraction, and fit any data-dependent quantity (margins, donor pools, character-name vocabulary, MLM/BT choices) using only the training portion of each of the five folds; validation folds remain original. Processing-time figures from round 0 are treated as unreliable, so cost is not used to rank families this round.

round_summary.round_hypothesis: Round 1's leading direction — cross-example recombination of a real utterance with a different same-label real context (P14, +0.0046 but inside its own noise_std 0.0068) — is provisionally the most promising mechanism, but it is confounded with augmentation dose (3.0x realized vs 1.46-2.15x for the arms it beat) and with the untested question of whether the sarcasm label actually travels with the utterance rather than with the pairing. This round tests (a) whether the grafting effect scales with copies/dose and survives a matched-dose cross-label control, and (b) whether other information sources the search has never touched — model-state difficulty (the missing P12 arm), the speaker attribute used additively instead of destructively, and embedding-similarity neighbours used for same-label text concatenation — can supply the decision-boundary information that uniform within-example replication demonstrably cannot.
round_summary.exploration_objective: Provisionally rank mechanisms by information source rather than by operator wording: recombination (scale + label-travel control), model-state selection (untested canonical), auxiliary speaker attribute injected rather than removed (untested canonical), similarity-based same-label text concatenation (untested canonical), plus a repair of the external-LLM family with label verification and a replication of the unresolved back-translation direction. All conclusions from rounds 0-1 are treated as provisional single-seed directions; no family is retired.
round_summary.strategy_selection_rationale: Follow-up on round 1: the recombination hypothesis was weakly supported (direction favourable, magnitude inside noise, dose-confounded) — addressed by P21 (dose refinement, multi-seed) and P22 (matched-dose cross-label control, the only way to separate 'label-consistent recombination' from 'more distinct rows'). The selection hypothesis was left untested because P12 never ran — re-instated as P23 at the exact substrate P13 showed to be F1-neutral, so the margin criterion is the only varying factor. The external-generation hypothesis was refuted at the measured level but with unverified labels — revisited as a repair (P26) that keeps only label-preserving rewrites plus a fold-internal verification filter, rather than discarding the family. Back-translation is unresolved (P04 +0.0016 single-seed vs P11 -0.0069 single-seed at 2.15x realized) — P27 replicates it at controlled dose and multiple seeds. Three families are new to the search: model-state difficulty (P23), speaker attribute as additive in-distribution evidence rather than anonymization (P24), and embedding-similarity same-label text concatenation (P25). Round-0's damaging arms (truncation, out-of-distribution placeholders, semantics-free noise) are deliberately not repeated. Every fitted quantity (SVM margins, embeddings, donor pools, few-shot exemplars) is fitted inside the training split of each CV fold only, and all arms declare their realized-dose design so yield confounds are visible.
round_summary.risk_profile: Conservative: P21, P27. Mid: P22, P23, P25. Higher-novelty: P24, P26.

round_summary.round_hypothesis: Provisional: the only direction with above-noise support is cross-example same-label context recombination (P14 -> P21, +0.0135 vs baseline at 4.0x, separated by ~0.024 from its dose-matched cross-label control). This round asks (a) what inside that family actually carries the gain — pairing diversity per row vs. row coverage, donor identity, replacement granularity, and whether the utterance's own context must be removed — and (b) whether other untested raw-text mechanisms (component-swapped recombination, within-example context restructuring) move the metric. All conclusions remain provisional: no variance estimate under matched seeds exists, and P21's delta is only ~1.5x its own noise_std.
round_summary.exploration_objective: Decompose the leading recombination family along mechanism-bearing axes (donor selection information source, splice granularity, replace-vs-add, coverage-vs-copies at matched 4.0x dose) while spending at least two arms on mechanisms never tested at raw-text level (donor-utterance component swap, context turn-order restructuring). Keep every arm inside the 2-4x multiplier constraint and inside the corpus's own surface distribution, since all train-only surface-rewriting arms (LLM, back-translation, speaker rendering) have lost 0.013-0.023 F1.
round_summary.strategy_selection_rationale: Follow-up on round 2's hypothesis: 'label-consistent cross-example recombination scales with dose' — provisionally supported, but confounded because copies_per_row and total multiplier were raised together, so P31 holds multiplier fixed at 4.0x and trades coverage for copies. P32 and P33 are not parameter tweaks: they change the information source used to pick donors (fold-internal embedding similarity) and the granularity of the splice (turn-level partial replacement), both untested. P34 and P35 are new families probing component specificity and within-example dialogue structure; P37 is a mechanistic control that adds donor context without deleting the row's own context, which distinguishes 'new pairings' from 'breaking the utterance-own-context association'. P36 tests whether an inert utterance-level edit dilutes or compounds the context-side gain at matched dose (round-2 lead 3). Utterance paraphrase/back-translation/LLM families are deprioritized, not retired, and get no standalone arm this round; they re-enter only inside P36 as a compounding probe. Distinctness is enforced everywhere by requiring donor_id != row_id and differing donor text, and by de-duplicating identical strings after generation. No arm alters class balance except P31, whose coverage change is stated explicitly.

round_summary.round_hypothesis: Round 3's premise that a specific sub-axis (component, donor similarity, granularity) of same-label context grafting carries the gain was refuted: utterance-swap (P34) matched context-swap (P21) at matched 4.0x, so the working mechanism is provisionally 'label-conditioned whole-component cross-example recombination' acting as an input-space regularizer, not incongruity modelling. Round 4 tests three things: (a) whether the mechanism is really about novel label-consistent (context,utterance) pairings rather than about row count/copies (near-identity dose control, dual-source double graft); (b) whether pairing novelty can be increased at the fixed 4x ceiling by mixing swap directions, decorrelating donor topics, or targeting rows the model actually gets wrong; (c) whether speaker coherence between grafted halves is a hidden requirement, which would also repair the twice-negative speaker-identity family.
round_summary.exploration_objective: Keep the leading recombination family under mechanistic pressure while spending at least half the budget on information sources it has never used (character/speaker metadata as a coherence constraint, fold-internal topic-cluster structure for anti-similar donor choice, fold-internal model state as a copy-allocation signal) and on the standing dose-vs-information confound. All conclusions from rounds 0-3 are treated as provisional; no family is retired, and the inert utterance-paraphrase, LLM and MT families are simply given zero budget this round rather than being declared failed.
round_summary.strategy_selection_rationale: All arms respect the 2-4x multiplier ceiling, so the dose curve cannot be extended upward; the remaining free levers at 4x are coverage, copies-per-row, donor choice and which fields are recombined. P41 (dual-source) is the higher-novelty canonical arm and is run unguarded at 4x. P42 mixes the two validated swap directions (additive vs saturating). P43 is the conservative refinement of the supported motif on the coverage axis flagged by P31. P44 is the missing confound control: a distinctness-preserving near-identity replication at the same 4x dose isolates 'more rows' from 'new pairings'; it is a confound isolation arm, not a variance probe. P45 revisits the speaker family in a controlled, in-distribution form where speaker renaming serves the grafting mechanism instead of standing alone. P46 reuses the model-state selection idea, which was previously only tested on the inert paraphrase substrate, on the substrate that actually works, with full coverage so selection changes copy allocation only. P47 attacks the mechanism hypothesis directly with topic-decorrelated donors, the opposite direction to P32's similarity ranking. Donor pools, clusters and margins are fitted on the training portion of each CV fold only. Grafting copies inherit the source row's label, so class balance is unchanged (no target-distribution shift); P46 changes only per-row copy allocation, which is stated as an induced coverage difference.

round_summary.round_hypothesis: Round 4's hypothesis that novelty levers (donor engineering, mixed swap directions, difficulty allocation) would push the label-conditioned whole-component grafting family past ~0.727 was not supported: all variants clustered inside their own noise bands, while the P44 dose control (0.7059) supported the sub-hypothesis that novel label-consistent (context,utterance) pairings, not row count, are the active ingredient. Round 5 therefore treats the grafting family as plateaued under its current parameterisation and asks three provisional questions: (1) does the benefit already saturate at the minimum admissible dose (2x, one grafted variant per row), which would improve both secondary metrics for free; (2) is there an untested recombination granularity or information source (multi-donor context assembly, class-prior-conditioned copy allocation, speaker-metadata-conditioned donor pools) that moves beyond the plateau; (3) where does the sarcasm label actually live — the utterance or the preceding context — which the cross-label control P22 could not answer because it assigned the utterance's label by construction.
round_summary.exploration_objective: Stage is exploration, so all conclusions here are provisional and no family is retired. Objective: spend one conservative refinement on the low end of the supported grafting dose curve, one repair on the thrice-negative speaker-identity family in its minimal (fields-only) form, and at least half the budget on mechanisms/information sources never tested — multi-donor turn-slot assembly, class-prior-conditioned copy allocation, speaker-metadata donor conditioning, and a target-transforming label-locus diagnostic. All arms stay inside the mandated 2-4x multiplier band and all fitted quantities (donor pools, class priors, speaker indexes) are built only from the training portion of each of the five folds.
round_summary.strategy_selection_rationale: P51 is the conservative refinement of the one motif with repeated above-baseline support, testing saturation at 2.0x rather than adding another 4x variant (history already covers 3x/4x/6.94x indistinguishably). P52 opens a new granularity/information source: contexts assembled slot-wise from several same-label donors, which is distinct from P33's own+single-donor hybrid splice (failed) and from P41's dual-donor whole-field composition (parity with best). P53 repairs the unresolved P45 confound by remapping only the context_speakers field with in-text mentions untouched, isolating 'speaker coherence is irrelevant' from 'name substitution corrupted the text'. P54 uses class priors, an information source never touched in five rounds, and explicitly declares the induced class-balance shift. P55 is the higher-novelty, target-transforming arm: dose-matched to P22 but assigning the donor context's label, which is the only way to test whether the label travels with the context; it is a diagnostic whose negative outcome is as informative as a positive one. P56 conditions the donor pool on speaker metadata, an axis distinct from the twice-deprioritised topic/TF-IDF donor engineering. Two arms at most (P51, P52) touch the grafting family's own parameters; the rest vary mechanism, information source, or target dependence. Timing is expected to stay near-zero for every arm, so the F1-first priority is not traded against processing time this round.

round_summary.round_hypothesis: Round 5's two provisional signals were (i) dose saturation of same-label context grafting at the minimum 2.0x point (P51) and (ii) a single above-plateau arm from speaker-metadata donor conditioning (P56, +0.0046 vs history best, ~1.0 noise_std, fallback rate unreported). This round follows up both: it crosses speaker conditioning with the saturated minimum dose, tests whether tighter pragmatic-coherence conditioning moves the metric monotonically, and — because the grafting plateau has absorbed most of the budget for three rounds — opens three mechanisms/information sources the search has never used: structural (turn-count/length) donor matching, class-prototype contexts, whole-context dropout, and target-conditioned cue statistics driving utterance-side cross-example lexical recombination. All conclusions are provisional; exploration stage, single-seed, no family is retired here.
round_summary.exploration_objective: Keep at least half the budget on previously untouched mechanisms and information sources (structural metadata, class prototypes, context removal, fold-internal label-cue statistics on the diagnostic utterance channel) while resolving whether the P56 speaker-conditioning direction is real and dose-independent rather than a fallback-diluted single point.
round_summary.strategy_selection_rationale: P61 and P62 are the only two variants of the metadata-conditioned donor family (min-dose cross and stricter-coherence), both instrumented with the fallback-rate diagnostic that was missing in P56, so its confound can be attributed next round. P63/P64 attack donor selection from information sources never tried (structural shape; per-label prototype contexts) after lexical-similarity (P32) and topic-distance (P47) donor engineering both failed, testing whether pragmatic/structural plausibility rather than content similarity is the useful axis. P65 is the deliberate higher-risk arm: if grafting works as a context-invariance regularizer, full context removal is the strongest form of that signal — P07's fixed-window truncation is a different, milder operator and its negative result does not settle removal. P66 addresses the round-5 lead that the label-bearing utterance channel has never been augmented in a label-aware way: it recombines non-cue content across same-label utterances while freezing fold-internal top-PMI sarcasm cues, which is mechanistically unlike the inert WordNet/back-translation/LLM rewriting arms (cross-example lexical source, cue-protected). All pools, statistics and prototypes are fitted on the training split of each CV fold only; all realized multipliers are inside the 2-4x band; every arm deduplicates generated rows against originals and each other, resampling donors on collision.

round_summary.round_hypothesis: The grafting gain is a context-invariance regularizer whose strength is governed by donor-pool entropy (number of distinct label-consistent contexts each utterance is paired with) rather than by donor plausibility; if so, an explicitly balanced context/label decorrelation should reach or exceed the ~0.723-0.731 plateau, and plausible out-of-corpus contexts should reproduce part of it. Round 6's follow-up question (is P56's speaker-conditioning gain real and dose-independent?) was left unresolved: P61 (2x) fell to baseline and P62 (stricter constraint, 4x) fell 0.0086 below P56, but dose and constraint were varied together and the promised fallback diagnostic was never reported, so realized constraint strength is unknown.
round_summary.exploration_objective: Resolve the speaker-conditioning constraint/coverage confound with an instrumented strict arm plus a coverage-matched uniform control; test the donor-entropy axis directly at fixed 4x; and spend half the budget on three mechanisms never tested at all (balanced context/label decorrelation pairs, cross-role transfer of donor target utterances into the context slot, and external out-of-corpus dialogue donors). All conclusions from prior rounds are treated as provisional single-seed observations on a plateau of width comparable to reported noise_std.
round_summary.strategy_selection_rationale: Every above-baseline result so far comes from one mechanism (label-preserving cross-example whole-component recombination), and refinements of its donor-selection rules (TF-IDF similar, topic-distant, addressee-coherent, prototype, structure-matched) have produced no movement beyond noise; per the budget policy this shifts weight toward mechanistically distinct directions. P71 and P72 attack the two unresolved confounds inside the leading family (donor entropy; constraint vs coverage in P56). P76 is the conservative refinement: the cheapest supported motif (structure-matched grafting, best F1/cost of round 6) pushed to an untested dose. P73, P74 and P75 open three untouched information sources/mechanisms: joint cross-example label structure, cross-role component placement, and external unlabeled dialogue. P73 and P75 deliberately relax the 'same-label donor' convention that P22/P55 made look mandatory: P22 biased every augmented row toward opposite-label contexts, whereas P73 pairs each donor context with both labels equally, which is a different construction, and P75 imports contexts that carry no corpus label at all. Each canonical arm is run at two settings spanning the admissible 2-4x band or at a mid-to-high setting; realized multipliers, donor-entropy and eligibility diagnostics must be reported per setting so that yield shortfalls seen in earlier rounds (P16, P43, P65, P66) do not recur as unattributable results.
